thread.title: Asian Stock Markets Choppy, Lower After Wall Street Gains

author: MT Newswires
title: Asian Stock Markets Choppy, Lower After Wall Street Gains
text:
Shutterstock photo Asian stock markets finished Wednesday unevenly, with some exchanges giving up ground after morning-session strength following Wall Street cues. Hong Kong and Shanghai declined, and Tokyo closed slightly in the green. Seoul's Kospi index fell back 2.31%, and other exchanges were mixed.
In Tokyo, the Nikkei 225 opened much higher, but lost ground in the afternoon session concluding the day up just 0.16%. Investors are still skittish about the prospects for higher global bond interest rates, which would drain capital out of equities markets, said analysts. Tokyo stocks fell by more than 7% in the first two trading days of the week.
In other news, real wages, adjusted for inflation, fell 0.5% in December from a year earlier, the labor ministry reported. Sluggish wages have undercut the Bank of Japan's goal of higher inflation and wages to boost the domestic economy, said analysts.
Also, Japan is expected to receive 3,000 cruise ships in 2018, about double the 2015 level, as Asian tourists flock to the island nation, reported The Nikkei financial news organization.
The benchmark Nikkei 225, up by more than 600 points in the morning session, finished up 35.13 to 21,546.37, as gaining issues outnumbered losers 110 to 108.
Leading the upside were silicon-wafer maker Sumco (SUMCF, 3436:Tokyo), up 6.7%, then Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHVYF, 7011:Tokyo), up 5.9%, and then Yokogawa Electric (YOKEY, 6841:Tokyo), up 5.1%.
On the downside were imaging house Ricoh (RICOY, 7752:Tokyo), off 6.6% and then Japan Tobacco (JAPAY, 2914:Tokyo), off 6.0% after reporting they will munch a new smokeless product.
The Hong Kong Hang Index opened higher on Wall Street cues, but could not hold onto gains and slipped to 0.89% in the red at the close of trading. Property stocks led the declines, as traders again exhibited concerns about rising global interest rates, said analysts. In addition, capital inflows through trading links connecting Hong Kong with stock exchanges in Shanghai and Shenzhen dried up.
The broad gauge Hang Seng fell 272.22 to 30,323.20, as losing issues outnumbered gainers 41 to right.
Leading the scant upside were diaper-maker Hengan International (1044:HK), up 1.8%, followed by confectioner Want Want China (151:HK), up 1.7%, and then Apple ( AAPL )-supplier AAC Technologies (2018:HK), up 1.2%.
On the downside were property concerns, China Resources Land (1109:HK), off 7.3%, and then China Overseas Land (688:HK), off 4.9%.
On the mainland, the Shanghai Composite fell 1.82% to 3,309.26.
On the other exchanges, the Taiwan TWSE gained 1.42%; the Australian ASX 200 inclined 0.75%; the Singapore Straits Times Index fell 0.66%; and the Thai Set fell 0.66%. In late trading in Mumbai, the Sensex was off 0.47%.
In other news, the Stock Exchange of Thailand plans to launch a board that lists securities of its less-developed neighboring countries, including Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar and Vietnam.
